discovered-from:LP-0MTZRM5HV0007S0V

The slot_schedule removal (LP-0MTZRM5HV0007S0V) removes the time-based slot schedule from proxy/config.yaml, config-fast.yaml, config-cheap.yaml.

The proxy-usage-analysis skill (.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/) still parses slot_schedule from the active config to derive per-time slot counts and ctx: scripts/config_loader.py (_normalize), scripts/bucketing.py (schedule_from_config), scripts/reporting.py (ctx_by_time), scripts/recommendations.py (advice pointing at 'proxy/config.yaml slot_schedule').

Impact: with no slot_schedule key, config_loader omits it and bucketing falls back to a single 'fast' bucket with default_slots (session_slot_pool_size) for the whole day — the cheap (2-slot) vs fast (3-slot) slot-count split is lost.

Required work (in the skill directory, per .pi boundary this item must be explicitly authorized):
- Derive per-mode slot counts from the mode profiles' static session_slot_pool_size (fast 3 / cheap 2) instead of schedule entries.
- Replace ctx_by_time semantics with the profiles' static local_model_ctx_size.
- Update recommendations text that references 'proxy/config.yaml slot_schedule'.
- Update skill tests/fixtures accordingly.

# Give the model (fallback chain) config control over the free-tier request budget

discovered-from:LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy operator, I want to set the free-tier request-budget behaviour
**per model / fallback chain** (with sensible global defaults), so I can tune
`plan`, `author`, `code` and `compact` independently — instead of every model
inheriting one global setting — while any single provider entry can still
override its own behaviour.

## Current state

- `rate_limit_rpm` is a **provider-entry** field (`provider_cfg`), so it is
  already configurable per entry — today only `munitoai-free` sets it (10).
- The four *behaviour* knobs are read **server-wide only**:
  `server.provider_rate_limit_reserve_ratio`,
  `server.provider_rate_limit_wait_max_seconds`,
  `server.provider_rate_limit_wait_max_waiters`,
  `server.provider_affinity_ttl_seconds`
  (`proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py::_config_value`, called with the server
  config).
- `acquire_provider_budget(provider_cfg, config, session_id, request)` is **not**
  given `model_config`/the model name, so a model-scoped setting cannot be
  expressed today — a single reserve ratio / wait cap applies to all chains.
- `affinity_ttl_seconds` is applied in three places, all of which read the same
  server config today: `acquire_provider_budget()`,
  `record_provider_affinity()` (via `provider.py::_maybe_record_provider_affinity`)
  and `provider_affinity_active()`. Honouring a model-scoped TTL (AC1) therefore
  requires threading the model config into the affinity record/lookup path too,
  not only into the acquire call.
- Both budget call sites in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` are
  `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (~line 7128) and
  `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` (~line 8141); each already holds the request's
  `model_config`.
- Consequence: an interactive chain (e.g. `plan`) and a background chain (e.g.
  `compact`) cannot trade latency against free-tier utilisation differently, and
  a future gated entry cannot be tuned without changing global behaviour.
- Caveat on `compact`: `models.compact` is consumed only by
  `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`, which dispatches to its providers
  directly over httpx and never calls the gate. A `models.compact.budget` block
  is therefore accepted and resolvable but has **no runtime effect** until that
  dispatch is gated (tracked separately — see OPEN QUESTION 1).

## Desired change

Add a **model-level `budget` block** with precedence
**provider entry > model block > server default > built-in default**:

```yaml
models:
  plan:
    budget:
      reserve_ratio: 0.4        # share of rate_limit_rpm reserved for in-progress
      wait_max_seconds: 10      # per-request wait cap for in-progress sessions
      max_waiters: 4            # concurrent waiter cap
      affinity_ttl_seconds: 600 # how long a session counts as in-progress
    providers:
      - name: munitoai-free
        rate_limit_rpm: 15      # entry-level override of the budget size
        budget:                 # optional per-entry behaviour override
          reserve_ratio: 0.2
```

- All five keys are optional at every layer; absent keys fall through to the next
  layer, so **existing configs behave exactly as today**.
- Values are clamped/validated exactly as the server-level knobs are today
  (ratio to `[0,1]`, wait/TTL to `>= 0`, malformed values fall back to the
  default with a warning — fail open, never fail closed).
- The effective values are visible per request in the budget logs/attempt
  diagnostics (which layer supplied `reserve_slots`/`effective_limit`), and the
  provider diagnostics table keeps showing remaining/limit per entry.
- The budget **bucket** remains keyed by provider entry (one account quota shared
  by `plan`/`author`/`code` even when their model blocks differ) — document this
  explicitly so per-model tuning is not mistaken for per-model quota.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `models.<name>.budget` block is honoured for `reserve_ratio`,
   `wait_max_seconds`, `max_waiters` and `affinity_ttl_seconds`, and a provider
   entry may override any of them with its own `budget` block.
2. Precedence is exactly entry > model > server > built-in default, proven by
   tests for every key (single-layer and multi-layer combinations).
3. Omitting all blocks reproduces today's behaviour byte-for-byte — identical
   `BudgetDecision` values (`reserve_slots`, `effective_limit`, `reason`) and
   identical log lines for the shipped `config.yaml` (no behavioural change;
   tested).
4. Malformed/out-of-range values fall back to the next layer with a logged
   warning and never raise or block a request (tests for each key).
5. The budget bucket stays shared per provider entry across models; a test proves
   two models with different `budget` blocks still consume one `rate_limit_rpm`
   window.
6. The effective configuration is visible in the budget skip/wait log lines and
   the attempt diagnostics (source layer included), and the provider diagnostics
   table keeps showing remaining/limit.
7. Tests cover both real fallback entry points —
   `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` —
   proving each passes the request's model config into the gate. (The intake's
   third clause, "the compaction/summarizer path where it reaches the same
   gate", is **not implementable as written**: `models.compact` is consumed only
   by `build_compact_summarizer()`, which calls providers directly over httpx
   and never reaches the gate. See OPEN QUESTION 1 and the follow-up item.)
8. Documentation updated: `proxy/config.yaml` header comments + a commented
   example, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`
   (model-level `budget` block alongside the `providers` list).
9. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Config-shape only: no change to gate semantics, reserve maths, or the
  affinity/wait design.
- Keep every layer optional; no migration of existing configs required.
- Do not introduce per-model *quota* (a separate budget per model) — that would
  break the one-account-per-entry model; if it is ever wanted, it must be a
  separate decision.
- The gate must remain fail-open when the new blocks are absent or malformed.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` — resolve each knob through the new
  entry > model > server precedence; extend `BudgetDecision`/logs with the source
  layer.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — pass `model_config` (and the model key) into
  `acquire_provider_budget()` from both fallback entry points
  (`_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle`, `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`) and into
  `_maybe_record_provider_affinity()` so the recorded TTL matches the model.
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` — precedence/validation/shared-bucket
  tests, plus the call-site wiring test (the module already imports
  `proxy.provider as provider`, so no new test module is needed).
- `proxy/config.yaml` — document the `models.<name>.budget` block; commented
  example.
- `proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py` + fixtures — only if the new keys are
  introduced as shipped values (they are optional; likely no fixture change).
- `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` — docs.

## Implementation order (test-first)

1. Add failing tests in `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` for precedence,
   validation/fallback and the shared-bucket guarantee (AC1–AC5).
2. Implement the layered resolver in `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py`
   (entry > model > server > built-in) and extend `BudgetDecision`/log lines
   with the source layer (AC6).
3. Thread `model_config` through both `provider.py` call sites and the affinity
   record/lookup path (AC1 `affinity_ttl_seconds`, AC7).
4. Update docs: `proxy/config.yaml`, `proxy/README.md`,
   `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` (AC8).
5. Run the suite via the test skill (AC9).

## OPEN QUESTIONS

1. **Compaction/summarizer path and the budget gate.** AC7 originally asked for
   coverage of "the compaction/summarizer path where it reaches the same gate".
   Fact check (this session): `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`
   (`build_compact_summarizer` / `_remote_chat_url`) resolves
   `models.compact.providers` itself and calls each provider **directly over
   httpx**, bypassing `localhost:8080` — so it never reaches
   `acquire_provider_budget()` and no `budget` block applies to it.
   AC7 was therefore narrowed to the two real fallback entry points and the gap
   was filed as `LP-0MVFYYYXS0011T58` (Gate the models.compact summarizer
   dispatch through the provider budget).
   **Preferred option (a): accept the split** — it preserves the "config-shape
   only" constraint and leaves eight of nine ACs unblocked; the summarizer gate
   is tracked separately. Alternative (b): widen this item to gate the
   summarizer dispatch as well (larger effort, and the `compact` half of the
   user story only becomes real then). Producer decision requested — see the
   comment on this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Is `rate_limit_rpm` used for any other provider (would per-model tuning
  matter beyond the free tier)?" Answer (Map, 2026-10-18, comment
  `LP-C0MVDVL1IR002EH5X`): no — `munitoai-free` is the only entry declaring it;
  the capability is dormant for every other provider, and the bucket is keyed by
  provider entry so `plan`/`author`/`code` share one 10/min window.
- Q: "Do both `provider.py` budget call sites have `model_config` available, and
  what are the functions called?" Answer (this session, code inspection): yes —
  `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` (~line 7128) and
  `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` (~line 8145); the AC7 name `_proxy_with_fallback`
  was corrected accordingly.
- OPEN QUESTION 1 (compaction/summarizer gate) — see above; needs a producer
  decision before the item is implemented. It does not block the other eight
  ACs.

## Related work

- `LP-0MVDUN5CY009VD20` — reserve + 15 s wait cap (introduced the knobs this item
  makes per-model).
- `LP-0MVDQ1GMO00801PL` — the original budget gate.
- `LP-0MVDVJYN5001BMG4` — evaluating whether the `munitoai-free` budget itself
  should be raised (the first consumer of per-model tuning).
- `LP-0MVDQKF4F008LGS6` — restricting the free tier to cheap mode (another
  model-scoped policy that could share this configuration shape).
- `LP-0MVDUZ0E10011W3C` (in progress) — rewrites the limiter/budget skip log
  lines that AC6 extends; sequence with it so the two log changes do not
  conflict.
- `LP-0MVDW6Z870066DEY` (open) — consolidating the fallback-chain configuration
  docs, of which the `budget` block docs (AC8) are one part.
- `LP-0MVF2DNCX003Z5CO` (in progress) — per-model context size, an existing
  example of a model-level knob read per request.
- Follow-up (filed this session) — `LP-0MVFYYYXS0011T58` — gate the
  `models.compact` summarizer dispatch so a `budget` block has runtime effect
  there.
data.title: Give the model/fallback-chain config control over free-tier budget knobs

# Intake Brief: Web UI to log input and output tokens (LP-0MVE592AU008VAP4)

## Headline

Display a cumulative, cross-request per-model token summary (input + output, broken down by category) in the existing `/logs` page summary header, using the current SSE token-snapshot and JSON-persistence plumbing.

---

## Problem Statement

The proxy's `/logs` page displays per-endpoint token totals and per-category breakdowns, but there is no view that aggregates token usage across all endpoints by LLM model. Operators cannot see how much each model is consuming overall — a key cost and capacity signal.

---

## Users

**Primary:** Proxy operators monitoring LLM proxy activity via the web log UI, diagnosing cost drivers and capacity allocation across models.

**User Stories:**
- As a proxy operator, I want a per-model running total of input (sent) and output (recv) tokens in the `/logs` summary header, so I can quickly see which models are consuming the most.
- As a proxy operator, I want each model's total broken down by category (User messages, Assistant, Tool Calls, System Prompt + Response), so I can attribute costs more precisely than a single aggregate number.
- As a proxy operator, I want the running totals to persist across proxy restarts, so I get a true long-term view rather than a reset-per-restart snapshot.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- The `/logs` page summary header displays a **per-model token section** (in addition to the existing per-endpoint section) showing:
  - One row per distinct model, with a total sent (input) and total recv (output) for that model.
  - Per-model category breakdown: User messages, Assistant (sent), Tool Calls (sent), System Prompt (sent), Response (recv).
  - Model names extracted from existing token-count keys (the `-> model:<name>` suffix already present in token-count keys such as `sent:user:POST /v1/chat/completions -> model:qwen3.6`).
- Running totals accumulate across requests and **persist across proxy restarts** via the existing `token_counts` JSON file (`proxy/logs/token_counts.json`).
- Category counts are consistent with the existing per-category breakdown keys (`sent:user:*`, `sent:assistant:*`, `sent:tool:*`, `sent:system:*`, `recv:response:*`) — no new token-counting logic is introduced.
- The per-model summary renders within the existing `renderSummary()` JavaScript function in `view_logs.html`, using the same SSE snapshot format (`{"tokens": {...}}`).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

---

## Constraints

- Must **reuse** the existing token-count key structure and SSE broadcast path — no new server-side token-counting logic.
- Must not break or double-count the existing per-endpoint display.
- Must handle the case where multiple endpoint paths share the same model name (aggregate correctly).
- Must be backward-compatible — no changes to the `token_counts` JSON schema; model grouping is a **UI-side** concern.

---

## Existing State

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — `srv.token_counts` dict holds keys like `sent:user:POST /v1/chat/completions -> model:qwen3.6`; `_increment_tokens()` updates these; `broadcast_status()` pushes snapshots via SSE.
- `proxy/templates/view_logs.html` — `renderSummary()` iterates endpoint defs and matches keys against endpoint paths; per-category breakdown already displayed per endpoint.
- Token counts are persisted to `proxy/logs/token_counts.json` (or `token_counts_filename`), loaded at startup via `load_token_counts()`.
- The model name is already encoded in token-count keys as the `-> model:<name>` suffix (visible in log output and keys).

---

## Desired Change

1. **Update `renderSummary()` in `view_logs.html`** to group token-count keys by model name (extract `-> model:<name>` from each key) and render a per-model table with sent/recv totals and category breakdowns.
2. **No server-side changes** — model grouping is a pure client-side aggregation over the existing token-snapshot data.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/templates/view_logs.html` — `renderSummary()` to add per-model section to summary header
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py` — No changes expected (existing SSE broadcast already carries per-key data)

---

## Related Work

| Item | Title | Relationship |
|------|-------|--------------|
| LP-0MRAW8XUF005IB4K | Token breakdown by category in session log display | Completed — established the per-category token-count keys and per-endpoint display this feature builds on |
| LP-0MQ0PYH8P008DLPJ | Web based logging per provider/model/session | Completed — parent of the log viewer feature set |
| LP-0MRAG775K008CKDG | Rethink logs display: remove model tabs, flat session list | Completed — current log viewer layout |

---

## Risks & Assumptions

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|-----------|
| Some token-count keys may lack the `-> model:` suffix (e.g. from legacy data or non-chat endpoints) | Keys without a model name are grouped under "unknown" with a debug log entry |
| Scope creep (adding per-model charts, export, or filters) | Record additional feature ideas as separate work items linked to this item |
| UI becomes crowded with many models | Use a scrollable card/container; add a "show fewer models" toggle if needed |

---

## Assumptions

- The model name in the key suffix is stable and sufficient for grouping (no need to fetch from a separate model-registry).
- The existing `token_counts` file is loaded at startup and retained across restarts — no migration needed.
- The proxy's `/logs` page is the sole UI target; no changes to the TUI footer or other dashboards.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1: "Where should the per-model running total appear?" — Answer (operator): **A — In the existing `/logs` page summary header, alongside the current per-endpoint display**. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q2: "What does 'running total' mean for persistence/scope?" — Answer (operator): **A — Cumulative since recording began, persisted across proxy restarts**. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
- Q3: "What granularity per model?" — Answer (operator): **B — Per-model totals broken down by category (user/assistant/tool/system) as well**. Source: interactive reply. Final: yes.
data.title: Web UI to log input and output tokens

# Automated tests: per-model token aggregation in /logs UI

## Summary

Playwright UI test for the per-model token summary section added to the `/logs` page summary header. Loads the page with an injected `window.__INITIAL_STATS` snapshot containing model-suffixed token-count keys (both `-> model:<name>` and bare `model:<name>` patterns, plus keys with no model suffix) and asserts the per-model aggregation renders correctly.

## Problem Statement

The per-model token summary (LP-0MVE592AU008VAP4) adds client-side aggregation logic to `renderSummary()` in `view_logs.html`. That logic must be verified automatically: correct per-model grouping, correct sent/recv and category totals, unknown-model fallback, and no regression of the existing per-endpoint display.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Playwright spec exists under `proxy/tests/` that loads the `/logs` page with an injected `window.__INITIAL_STATS` snapshot containing keys with `-> model:<name>` suffixes, bare `model:<name>` keys, and keys without any model suffix (e.g. `-> local`).
- The spec asserts one summary row per distinct model with correct total sent and total recv values.
- The spec asserts the per-model category breakdown (User / Assistant / Tool / System sent; Response recv) matches the fixture values.
- The spec asserts keys without a model suffix are grouped under an "unknown" model row rather than dropped.
- The spec asserts the existing per-endpoint token section still renders its correct values (no double-counting or breakage regression).
- The spec passes under the Playwright runner against the local proxy.

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/model-tokens.spec.js` — new Playwright spec
- `proxy/tests/slot-logs.spec.js` — pattern reference for fake SSE / injected stats
- `proxy/templates/view_logs.html` — subject under test (rendering)

## Assumptions

- The Playwright approach mirrors `slot-logs.spec.js` (page route interception / injected client state); a live or stubbed proxy is available as in existing specs.
- Test-only change; no production code modified in this work item.

# Remove stale REFACTOR markers when their work item closes

## Problem statement

The refactor skill injects `REFACTOR-<id>` marker comments into source files to suppress duplicate work-item creation, but there is no removal path: once the referenced smell is fixed (or judged a false positive) and its work item closes, the marker persists and — because `has_existing_comment(file_path, smell_type)` matches on *smell type* only — permanently suppresses detection of that smell type in that file.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `/skill:refactor` or the implement pipeline's refactor step — they trust duplicate suppression to be accurate; a stale marker silently hides a real regression.
- **Developers reading source files** — stale markers are noise that misrepresents outstanding work.
- **Producers triaging the Refactor backlog** — a closed work item should leave no trace in the codebase.

Example user stories:

- "As an agent running the refactor step, when a marker's work item is already closed, I want the marker gone (or ignored) so I do not skip a smell that has regressed."
- "As a developer, when a refactor item is completed or judged a false positive, I want its comment removed from the file without touching surrounding code or line endings."
- "As a producer, I want a single command that reports every stale marker in the project and can clean them up."

## Existing state

- `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` provides `inject_refactor_comment()`, `has_existing_comment()`, `get_comment_style()` and `_build_comment_block()`; there is **no removal function**.
- Two slightly different regexes parse markers: `comment_injection.REFACTOR_PATTERN` (`REFACTOR-(\S+).*?smell:\s*(\S+)`, DOTALL) and `workitem_creation.REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN` (multi-line, expects a comment prefix before `smell:`).
- Markers are written in two shapes: line-prefixed (`# <!-- REFACTOR-…` … `# -->` for Python/YAML/shell, `// <!-- …` for JS/TS) and native block (`<!-- … -->` for Markdown/HTML). CSS-family files use `/* … */` with ` * ` prefixes.
- `inject_refactor_comment()` reads and writes text mode without `newline=""`, so injected files are normalised; removal must not repeat that mistake.
- `StatusLifecycle.show()` and `shared.status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags()` already provide safe work-item lookup and prefix-to-sibling worklog-store resolution. Verified: a bare `wl show <foreign-prefix-id>` fails ("Work item not found"), so a sweep **must** inject `--worklog-dir` from the shared resolver.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` `remediate_pre_existing()` injects markers only for smells it just filed items for; the pipeline syncs the worklog first (`wl sync --if-idle`) and has no post-close hook.
- The canonical source of the skill is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/` (symlinked into `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor`); its tests live in `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/`, with `tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` (1251 lines) covering the current API.
- Stale markers confirmed at HEAD in the `llm` repo (work-item state checked 2026-10-20):

| File | Marker | Item stage |
|---|---|---|
| `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` | open / `intake_complete` — reported false positive |
| `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py:8` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTHLGVPO004DZ56` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTGDB3D9007TWHA` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MVB0THT7000KT0G` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTV87EC4006EU5Z` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MTRWI65I005VXOC` | completed / `done` |
| `proxy/proxy/provider.py:2` | `REFACTOR-LP-0MSI4ZIF60064EOR` | completed / `done` |

- The same defect is visible in the `SorraAgents` repo itself: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (2 markers), `pi-client/voice-input/whisper_worker.py`, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_json_contract_reask.py` (3), `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (2), `skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_regressions.py` — 4 of these reference `completed` items, the rest reference `open / idea` items.

## Desired change

1. **Removal API** in `skill/refactor/comment_injection.py`: `remove_refactor_marker(file_path, work_item_id) -> dict` (or a small dataclass) that locates the whole marker block for that id — line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` shapes — and deletes it, leaving the remainder of the file byte-identical (including CRLF/LF and the file's original trailing newline). Absent marker → `{"removed": False, "reason": "absent"}`; repeated runs are no-ops.
2. **Sweep module** (new `skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py`): discover markers in repo-tracked files (exclude `.worklog/`, `node_modules`, binaries), group by referenced work-item id to one `wl show` per distinct id (worklog dir resolved via `shared.status_lifecycle.resolve_worklog_flags`), classify each marker as `stale` (stage `in_review`/`done`/`completed` or status `completed`), `active` (any other resolved stage) or `unknown` (lookup failed), and return a structured report.
3. **Trigger** from the refactor pipeline: run the sweep after the `wl sync` and **before** smell detection, so `has_existing_comment` never observes a stale marker. Non-fatal on `wl` failure (log a warning, keep markers). Standalone CLI entry point (`--sweep-markers`, report-only by default, `--apply` to delete) and a skip flag (`--no-marker-sweep`).
4. **`has_existing_comment` correctness**: keep it a pure file predicate by default, but accept an optional `is_active` resolver/callback so a caller can exclude terminal items; the pipeline's sweep-before-detect ordering is what makes the default path correct. `unknown` markers keep suppressing (conservative) and are reported as warnings.
5. **False-positive path**: a marker whose item is still open but was judged a false positive must be removable explicitly (`--remove-marker <work-item-id>` or `remove_refactor_marker()` called directly), independent of item stage.
6. **Unit tests** in `tests/test_refactor/`: removal for `#`, `//`, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` shapes; block and line-prefix styles; CRLF preservation; absent-marker no-op; idempotent re-run; multi-marker file touching only the target block; classification of `in_review`/`done`/`completed`/`open`; `unknown` id kept and reported; dry-run performs no writes; cross-store id resolution.
7. **Sweep the existing stale markers** in `llm` (6 stale; the false positive needs an explicit decision) and in `SorraAgents` (4 stale), so `grep -rn "REFACTOR-"` afterwards shows only markers whose items are non-terminal.
8. **Documentation**: `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` (§ REFACTOR Comments + flags table + report keys), `docs/refactor.md` (§ 4 Work Item Creation, troubleshooting "Duplicate work items created", module reference), and module docstrings. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (ship pipeline owns it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `remove_refactor_marker()` removes a `REFACTOR-<id>` marker block (line-prefixed, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles) from a file while leaving all surrounding content byte-identical and preserving the file's line endings (verified by a CRLF fixture test).
- [ ] Removal is a no-op (`removed=False`) when the marker is absent, and re-running it is idempotent.
- [ ] A sweep reports every marker in the project with its referenced item's stage and a classification of `stale` / `active` / `unknown`; removal is triggered for markers whose work item is at a terminal stage (`in_review`, `done`, `completed`).
- [ ] Sweep work-item lookups resolve the correct worklog store via the shared resolver (a foreign-prefix id resolves; failure is non-fatal and keeps the marker as `unknown`).
- [ ] `has_existing_comment()` no longer suppresses detection for closed work items — covered by a test asserting a terminal-stage marker is not treated as an existing comment on the sweep-before-detect path (and via the optional active-item filter).
- [ ] An explicit false-positive removal path exists for markers whose work item is still open, with `--dry-run` making no writes.
- [ ] Running the sweep (apply mode) removes the 6 stale `llm` markers listed above and the 4 stale `SorraAgents` markers; a follow-up `grep -rn "REFACTOR-"` shows only markers whose items are non-terminal.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: `#`, `//`, `<!-- -->` and `/* */` styles; absent marker; idempotent re-run; multi-marker file; terminal vs non-terminal classification; unknown id; dry-run no-write.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Canonical source is `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/`; never edit `~/.pi/agent/skills/...` (the installer replaces it) and never hand-edit markers in `llm` outside an authorised implementation run.
- Standard library only — no new third-party dependencies.
- One `wl show` per distinct referenced work-item id (cached per run); the sweep must stay in the same sub-second-to-low-seconds envelope as the existing pipeline rather than spawning per marker.
- Sweep is read-only unless `--apply` (or the default pipeline policy) removes stale markers; `--dry-run` must never write.
- Never remove a marker for an item that is not terminal unless explicitly requested by id.
- Only scan git-tracked files in the repo root (skip `.worklog/`, worktrees, `node_modules`, binary files).
- Work-item ids may belong to sibling project stores; always route `wl` through the shared resolver, not the cwd default.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/comment_injection.py` — add `remove_refactor_marker()`, a single tolerant marker parser covering both existing regexes, `is_active` filter hook on `has_existing_comment()`, and `newline=""` IO.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/marker_sweep.py` (new) — marker discovery, per-id work-item lookup via `shared.status_lifecycle`, classification and report structure.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — sweep step after `wl sync` / before detection, `--sweep-markers`, `--apply`, `--remove-marker`, `--no-marker-sweep` flags, report keys.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — reuse the unified marker pattern instead of its own `REFACTOR_COMMENT_PATTERN`.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — marker lifecycle and new flags.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/docs/refactor.md` — § 4, troubleshooting, module reference.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_comment_injection.py` — extend with removal tests.
- `~/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/test_marker_sweep.py` (new) — sweep classification, dry-run, unknown ids, non-fatal wl failures.
- `llm`: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_config.py`, `proxy/tests/test_cold_start_immunity.py`, `proxy/tests/test_compaction_logger_hierarchy.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`, `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — sweep targets only (no hand edits).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Repository placement (assumption A1):** the skill's source of truth is `SorraAgents`, so the code change belongs there with its own `SA-` work item; this `LP-` item then owns the `llm` sweep. Risk: `implement.py` creates worktrees from the cwd's `.worklog`, so an `LP-` item cannot host edits under `~/projects/SorraAgents`. Needs producer confirmation (Q1).
- **No close hook:** `wl` exposes no plugin/hook on close (only `wl plugins` for discovery), so "triggered when the item reaches a terminal stage" is implemented as a sweep at refactor-run time plus a standalone command — not an event. Assumption A2.
- **False-positive regression loop:** removing the marker for a closed false-positive item re-enables detection, so the next scan re-files the same item. Mitigation: false positives must be closed with a reason *and* either fixed or excluded via `.refactor.json`/per-file ignore; the sweep should report (not silently hide) this case. Scope-creep risk — an ignore-list mechanism is a separate work item.
- **Mixed answers to `unknown`:** unresolvable ids (deleted items, wrong store) could hide real work. Conservative default: keep + warn.
- **Formatting churn:** a naive implementation strips a leading blank line or rewrites CRLF files, producing whole-file diffs. Byte-preserving IO (`newline=""`, explicit trailing-newline handling) plus a CRLF fixture test is mandatory.
- **Regex divergence:** the two existing patterns disagree on block styles; unifying them is required or Markdown/CSS markers will be missed by the sweep.
- **Scope creep:** generalising to a lifecycle framework for all agent-injected comments is out of scope; record as a separate item if it surfaces.

## Open questions

1. **Repository and work-item placement** — implement in `~/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor` under a new `SA-` item (this `LP-` item keeps the `llm` sweep and records the blocker), or keep everything under this `LP-` item and treat the SorraAgents edits as out-of-worktree?
2. **Trigger surface** — sweep automatically inside the refactor pipeline (default) plus a standalone `--sweep-markers --apply`, or standalone-only (manual/cron)?
3. **False positives and unresolvable ids** — should `has_existing_comment` keep suppressing on `unknown` ids (conservative) while a manual `--remove-marker <id>` handles false positives, or should both be dropped automatically?

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Which repository should host the skill change — `SorraAgents/skill/refactor` (canonical source, its own `SA-` item) or this `LP-` item in `llm`?" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor`; the skill's tests live in `SorraAgents/tests/test_refactor/`; `implement.py` creates worktrees from the cwd's `.worklog`, so an `LP-` item cannot legally host edits under `SorraAgents`. **Recommended:** new `SA-` item in `SorraAgents` for the skill change, `LP-0MVF4OPC1001RYX6` scoped to the `llm` marker sweep and recording the blocker.
- Q: "How should the terminal-stage trigger be implemented, given `wl` exposes no close hook?" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: `wl plugins` only lists plugins; no event/hook surface found; the refactor pipeline already runs at the end of implementation and syncs first. **Recommended:** sweep inside the refactor pipeline (after `wl sync`, before detection) plus a standalone `--sweep-markers` report/`--apply` CLI.
- Q: "Should markers referencing unresolvable work items, and false-positive markers whose item is still open, be removed automatically?" — **OPEN QUESTION**. Research: all `llm` markers resolve today except none; `LP-0MVDFQC2X005S7WE` is open at `intake_complete` while the marker is documented as a false positive. **Recommended:** keep `unknown` markers and warn; require an explicit `--remove-marker <id>` for open-item false positives.

# Gate the `models.compact` summarizer dispatch through the provider budget

discovered-from:LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV

## Problem

`models.<name>.budget` (LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV) makes the free-tier request-budget
behaviour configurable per model. That only works for requests that go through
the provider fallback chain in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`.

`models.compact` is the exception: `proxy/proxy/compaction_summarizer.py`
(`build_compact_summarizer()`, `_compact_model_config()`, `_remote_chat_url()`)
resolves the chain itself and calls each provider entry **directly over httpx**,
bypassing `localhost:8080`. It therefore never reaches
`acquire_provider_budget()`, so a `models.compact.budget` block — or an entry
`rate_limit_rpm` on a `compact` provider — has no runtime effect. The
per-model-tuning goal explicitly names `compact` as a chain the operator wants
to tune, so this gap is material.

## Desired change

Decide and implement one of:

1. Gate the summarizer dispatch: call
   `acquire_provider_budget(provider_cfg, config, session_id=None, request=None)`
   before each summarizer tier attempt (a summarizer call has no session
   affinity, so it is always treated as a *new* session — pass through rather
   than wait, honouring the per-model `budget` block), and record the outcome in
   the summarizer attempt diagnostics.
2. Or document explicitly (in `proxy/docs/routing.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md`)
   that `models.compact` is not budget-gated and that a `budget` block there is
   inert, and drop `compact` from the stated tuning scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. If option 1: a gated `compact` provider entry is skipped (not dispatched) once
   its `rate_limit_rpm` window is full, and the summarizer falls through to the
   next tier (or returns `EmptySummary` when all tiers are gated) without raising.
2. If option 1: `models.compact.budget` values are honoured for the summarizer
   dispatch and the effective source layer appears in the summarizer attempt
   diagnostics.
3. If option 2: `proxy/docs/routing.md` and `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` state that the
   summarizer bypasses the budget gate.
4. Behaviour is unchanged when no `rate_limit_rpm`/`budget` block is configured
   on the `compact` chain (fail-open).
5. Tests cover the chosen behaviour (gated skip + fall-through, or the documented
   exemption).

## Notes

- Depends on the layered resolver from LP-0MVDVK5TM004TQQV (do that item first).
- No per-model *quota*: the bucket stays keyed by provider entry.
